title: Beyond Consultation: Why Civil Society Must be at the Centre of Development Efforts
content:
By Mr. Mandeep S. Tiwana, Secretary General, CIVICUS, Mr. Luca De Fraia, Deputy Secretary-General, ActionAid Italy and Ms. Nurgul Dzhanaeva, President of the Forum of Women’s NGOs of Kyrgyzstan

Country ownership is needed for sustainable development. Yet the civic space is closing.  

At a time when the world faces multiple intersecting crises such as violent conflict, rising inequality, climate vulnerability and reversals of hard-won gains on gender justice and human rights, effective development co-operation has never been more important. Closing civic space and declining trust in institutions are accentuating these challenges.

The latest monitoring results from the Global Partnership for Effective Development Co-operation’s (GPEDC) Making Development Co-operation More Effective 2026 Progress Report highlight that much more must be done to ensure that civil society organisations are genuinely empowered as development partners, including through enabling civic space conditions and meaningful opportunities to participate in decision-making.

title: What We Heard From the Creative Commons Community
content:
It’s a question we ask ourselves regularly at CC—and one we recently brought directly to our community through our annual Community Survey. This year, 62 community members from 23 countries shared their experiences, priorities, ideas, and hopes for the future of the Commons.

What we heard most clearly is that you want  to participate. You want to learn from one another, contribute your skills, build relationships across regions and areas of practice, and help shape the future of the open movement. 

The survey gave us a clear picture of what meaningful participation means to you, what the barriers are, and what CC can do to help. Here’s what we heard and how it’s shaping our plans for the year ahead. 

A community that wants to participate

Overall satisfaction with the CC community increased this year, reaching 3.8 out of 5—up 19% from 2025. Sixty-four percent of respondents rated their engagement with the community a 4 or 5, and 60% said you would recommend the CC community to others.

Perhaps most encouragingly, half of you said you were interested in participating in self-led activities like ad-hoc working groups.

title: October Office Hour
content:
In this office hour, we will take a closer look at DRP's Baserow Tracker–used to create records for rescued datasets–and how to prepare data for batch import into the tracker. There will be a brief introduction to the backend tables, followed by a review of DRP's new batch import guide and template. Using the example of a batch import, we will demonstrate how to use the popular open source data wrangling tool OpenRefine for common metadata tasks.

All volunteers are welcome to join! This office hour will be particularly useful for volunteers engaged in batch-rescuing datasets who want to learn how to prepare their spreadsheet data for import into the DRP Tracker. It is also intended for those interested in learning about OpenRefine.

The office hour will be led by DRP's Metadata Specialist Karen Hwang, who has been using OpenRefine for a variety of projects since 2014, including large-scale migrations between repositories, linked open data creation to promote interoperability, and evaluating inventories to support archival arrangement.

content: As we continue our coverage on the rise of right-wing political parties across Europe, we speak to Wiebke Judith from the German organization for asylum seekers’ rights, PRO ASYL, about Germany’s far-right party Alternative für Deutschland, or AfD, and its recent wins in September’s state elections. Judith calls the historic wins — won by margins not seen in German elections since the Nazi era — “deeply concerning for everyone who cares about our democracy,” and says that the growing influence of the AfD’s anti-immigration stance over the German political landscape poses grave risks to refugees, asylum seekers, immigrants and ethnic minorities in the country.

title: We Demand More Information on How Marin Cops Illegally Shared Flock ALPR Data
content:
The Marin County Sheriff’s Office is the latest California law enforcement agency to get caught sharing automated license plate reader (ALPR) data from their Flock Safety system with out-of-state and federal agencies. EFF and the ACLU of Northern California are calling them out for this direct violation of California law, which has put every driver in the county at risk and is especially dangerous for immigrants, abortion seekers, and other targets of the federal government.

Today, we sent the Marin County Sheriff’s Office (MCSO) a demand letter and request for records under the California Public Records Act following the Point Reyes Light’s recent report that MCSO provided non-California agencies access to its ALPR database. This directly violates California law and the terms of the 2022 Settlement Agreement in our case Lagleva v. Marin County Sheriff.

ALPRs are cameras that capture images of vehicles and upload their location to a searchable, shareable database. They are a mass surveillance technology that collects data indiscriminately on every vehicle on the road.

title: Osakesäästötilin laajentaminen rahastoihin ei vaaranna valtion verotuloja
content:
Osakesäästötilin kohdevalikoiman laajentaminen pörssiosakkeista sijoitusrahastoihin ei merkittävästi leikkaisi Suomen verotuloja, arvioidaan Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitoksen tuoreessa selvityksessä. Mahdollinen verotuottojen menetys jäisi arviolta 1–5 miljoonaan euroon vuodessa. Koska rahastojen kasvuosuuksiin liittyy jo nykyisellään verotuksen lykkääntymisetu, sijoittajilla olisi vain vähän taloudellisia kannustimia siirtää nykyisiä rahastosijoituksiaan osakesäästötilille.

Vuonna 2020 käyttöön otetun osakesäästötilin tavoitteena on ollut edistää kotitalouksien aktiivista säästämistä ja sijoittamista. Tilin hyödyntäminen on kuitenkin jäänyt odotettua vähäisemmäksi: vuoden 2024 lopussa aktiivisia osakesäästötilejä oli 260 tuhatta kappaletta ja niiden käypä arvo oli 2,9 miljardia euroa.

title: The Buzludzha Monument, Bulgaria: How to transform contested heritage into a place for dialogue, education and culture
content:
Built in 1981 as the House-Monument of the Bulgarian Communist Party, the Buzludzha Monument in the mountains of central Bulgaria is one of the most striking examples of 20th-century architecture in the country. Following the end of the Communist regime in 1989, the building was abandoned and has since suffered from theft, vandalism and severe weather conditions. Its windows and roof have been severely damaged, leaving the structure exposed to the elements and putting its remarkable interior mosaics at increasing risk. The Buzludzha Monument was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2018 by Europa Nostra.

Since its involvement in the 7 Most Endangered Programme, the Buzludzha Monument has gained increasing international attention and momentum towards its conservation and sustainable future. The Buzludzha Project Foundation has advocated for its stabilisation, preservation and interpretation, with the ambition of demonstrating how difficult and contested heritage can be responsibly conserved and understood.

title: SMUGGLAREN – specialvisning
content:
Datum: 20 oktober
Tid: kl. 18.00
Plats: Folkets Hus Kallhäll
Biljetter: Bio.se

Träffa regissören och filmens huvudperson Smugglerskan i samband med specialvisningen av den prisbelönta dokumentären Smugglaren! 

Kort om filmen

På jakt efter en försvunnen revolver kliver en envis pensionär ombord på en terapibuss som tar henne på en oförglömlig resa genom Finland.

Den nyblivna pensionären Lisbeth ger sig ut på sitt livs viktigaste uppdrag: att hitta pistolen som hennes far riktade mot sig själv år 1940, men misslyckades att ta sitt liv med. Vapnet försvann och blev med tiden en mörk familjelegend.

Fast besluten att föra vapnet hem till Sverige stiger hon ombord på en terapibuss tillsammans med andra anhöriga till krigsveteraner. Det blir en känslomässig resa genom Finland, där Lisbeth möter en vapenhandlare, lär sig skjuta och lever ut sina drömmar, allt under vägledning av en mystisk häxa.

Ju närmare bussen kommer den ryska gränsen, desto närmare kommer Lisbeth inte bara den försvunna pistolen, utan också en försoning med sin far, sitt förflutna och ett land märkt av krig.

Smugglaren vann Best Nordic Documentary Award på Nordisk Panorama 2026.

title: Lokakuun apurahahaku nykytaiteen kansainvälisiin hankkeisiin 2026–2027
content:
Framen lokakuun apurahahaku suomalaisen nykytaiteen kansainvälisiin hankkeisiin on käynnistynyt 1. lokakuuta 2026. Lokakuun hakukierroksella on haettavissa kaksi eri apurahatyyppiä: liikkuvuusapuraha matka- ja kuljetuskuluihin sekä tuotantoapuraha kansainvälisiin teostuotantoihin.

Framen apurahoilla tuetaan suomalaisten ja Suomessa työskentelevien nykytaiteilijoiden, taiteen asiantuntijoiden ja taideorganisaatioiden kansainvälistymistä. Apurahoilla tuetaan teosten esittämistä ja teostuotantoja ulkomailla sekä osallistumista ammattilaistapahtumiin. Kaikissa kategorioissa apurahoja voivat hakea yksittäiset taiteilijat ja taiteen asiantuntijat, työryhmät sekä rekisteröidyt yhteisöt.

Vuoden kolmas hakukierros on avoinna 1.–31.10.2026, jolloin apurahat ovat haettavissa vuosina 2026–2027 toteutuviin hankkeisiin. Haku sulkeutuu lauantaina 31. lokakuuta 2026 kello 23.59 Suomen aikaa.

Framen toimiala on visuaalinen taide, painottuen erityisesti nykytaiteeseen. Toiminnan piiriin kuuluvat myös poikkitaiteelliset muodot, kuten ääni-, performanssi- ja installaatiotaide, silloin kun ne esitetään nykytaiteen kontekstissa. Framen apurahoilla tuetaan myös sarjakuvataidetta ja taidekäsityötä.

title: The sound of resistance
content:
A collaborative piece about different forms of protest music across time and geography

Originally published on Global Voices

Image courtesy of Sydney Allen. Made via Canva Pro.

This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.

For nearly as long as there have been governments and a ruling class, there has been music aimed at mocking them, demanding change, and airing grievances. Music can be a powerful form of resistance — particularly in anti-democratic contexts where direct action can be risky. Music offers people a way to subvert those in power, connect with others on an emotional level, and a catchy, memorable tune can spread faster than any political speech or slogan.

title: How do you know when AI is wrong? Lessons from our forum at The New York Times
content:
AI is opening up stories that were too big to report by hand, from millions of pages of Epstein files to hundreds of hours of podcasts, and it's making investigative reporters rethink how they check their work. That was one of the threads through our AI x Investigative Journalism Forum at The New York Times, where about 150 journalists and technologists heard speakers from The Times, The Associated Press, NPR, Reuters, ABC News and CNN share what worked, what didn't and how they test the results before running a story.

Plus: The Times team who built their "Epstein Files Engine" wrote up what they learned in a new paper. Our AI Papers Explained breaks it down, including why they say their verification standard “worked precisely because most leads did not survive it.”

title: A Council of Warnings in a World at War
content:
From Ukraine and Myanmar to Haiti, the final days of September showed why the United Nations remains necessary and why its decisions so often fall short.

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | NEW YORK | 1 October 2026 (IDN) — The United Nations Security Council ended on 30 September with a record that was neither empty nor reassuring. It brought the war in Ukraine before ministers, kept diplomatic channels open during a dangerous confrontation involving Iran, renewed international action against armed groups in Haiti and condemned a deadly air strike in Myanmar. At the same time, the UN refugee agency warned that severe funding shortages could deprive 8.3 million displaced people of essential help.

Taken together, these events offered a clearer measure of the UN than either its defenders or its critics usually allow. The organisation remains the only chamber in which adversaries, large and small states and affected countries can place their claims before the world. It can define legal obligations and authorise collective action, but it cannot make governments supply troops, money or political consent. The distance between decision and result becomes painfully visible.
snippet:
From Ukraine and Myanmar to Haiti, the final days of September showed why the United Nations remains necessary and why its decisions so often fall short.

By Ramesh Jaura

title: Beyond publication: How watchdog journalism makes a difference
content:
What do the 2026 IJ4EU Impact Awards reveal about the ambitions, pressures and responsibilities of investigative journalism in Europe?

A doctor sanctioned in one country resumes practising in another. A chemical factory closes in Europe, only to reappear thousands of kilometres away. Industry lobbying shapes a regulatory debate with little public scrutiny. A photograph celebrated by journalism’s own institutions carries a false description of a murdered man for three decades.

The investigations recognised at IJ4EU’s 2026 Impact Awards exposed very different failures. Taken together, they offer a revealing picture of the work independent investigative journalism is being asked to do: follow problems beyond the boundaries of national oversight, test the claims of powerful interests and dig into uncomfortable truths.

They also raise a question that extends well beyond an awards ceremony. What should count as evidence that this work matters?

“Our discussions kept returning to one deceptively simple question,” said jury chair Leila Bičakčić, co-founder and executive director of the Center for Investigative Reporting in Sarajevo. “What do we mean when we say that journalism has impact?”
snippet: What do the 2026 IJ4EU Impact Awards reveal about the ambitions, pressures and responsibilities of investigative journalism in Europe?

title: COMMUNIA Salon: Time to fix copyright
content:
The Commission has put copyright back on the menu. This is a chance to remove longstanding issues, but will the initiative address all of them?

Join COMMUNIA on Wednesday, 7 October, at 15:00 CEST for a special online salon to explore that question. We will share our first assessment of the recently opened public consultation and discuss the changes needed to support research, public-interest AI and the knowledge institutions on which both depend.

Building on the call for evidence before the summer break, the consultation addresses four areas: copyright and generative AI; online piracy of time-sensitive copyright-protected content; the use in the EU of sound recordings by nationals of non-EU countries; and copyright and research. The salon will concentrate on generative AI and research, where reform could make a significant difference to how knowledge is accessed, shared and used.

title: Kun aseet eivät kiinnosta, tie vie kirjastoon
content:
Elias Ojalammi on yksi lukuisista nuorista, jotka päättivät suorittaa siviilipalveluksensa kirjastossa.

19-vuotias Ojalammi kertoo, että hänelle kyse oli sekä arvovalinnasta että käytännön syistä. Armeija ei kiinnostanut häntä, eivätkä myöskään aseet.

”Se on arvokysymys, mutta tämä sopii myös paremmin aikatauluuni. Tästä on minulle myös enemmän hyötyä, sillä saan työkokemusta”, Ojalammi sanoo.

Ojalammi tekee kirjastossa perustyötä, kuten asiakaspalvelua, hyllytystä, tapahtumissa avustamista sekä logistiikkaan liittyviä tehtäviä. Tehtäviin on kuulunut esimerkiksi digiopastusta.

Ojalammi pitää kirjastotyön vahvuutena sen monipuolisuutta. Päivittäin hän siirtyy tehtävästä toiseen ja pääsee kartuttamaan osaamistaan eri asioissa. Käytännön työn ohella hän oppii asiakaspalvelua.

Lapinjärvellä sijaitsevassa Siviilipalveluskeskuksessa kirjastoja pidetään erittäin suosittuina ja merkittävinä siviilipalveluspaikkojen tarjoajina. Parhaillaan siviilipalvelusta suorittaa vajaat 800 siviilipalvelusvelvollista, joista noin sata on kirjastoissa.

Eniten siviilipalvelushenkilöitä rekrytoidaan pääkaupunkiseudun kirjastoihin. Palvelusvelvollisia on myös yliopistokirjastoissa.

title: Choose Europe… or Are Research & Science Better Supported by Copyright Laws Elsewhere?
content:
Europe fails researchers in 7 cases.

Europe faces increasingly intense competition for research talent. The Choose Europe for Science initiative responds by helping attract and retain researchers and by promoting Europe’s strengths.

To improve Europe’s attractiveness compared to its competitors, decision-makers will also need to assess how we compare to other jurisdictions on copyright and how well Europe’s regime works for researchers.

There is still plenty to do!

Choosing Europe for science means choosing Europe for knowledge, too.

Click a case to expand. (Open all · Close all)

Israel, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Switzerland, Taiwan and the US all allow TDM on legally accessed materials in partnership with industry, bringing extra resources to research institutions.

In the EU and UK, commercial partners are excluded. Researchers must buy an additional licence for content they already legally access, if one exists at all, and publisher contracts increasingly even try to block non-commercial TDM, against EU law.

title: Kulttuuri kuuluu kaikille
content:
Kulttuuri ei ole harvojen harrastus eikä ylimääräinen menoerä, josta voidaan vaikeina aikoina huoletta tinkiä. Kirjat, musiikki, teatteri, museot, elokuvat, tapahtumat ja kirjastot ovat osa ihmisten arkea, hyvinvointia ja sivistystä. Kulttuuri tarjoaa elämyksiä, mutta auttaa myös ymmärtämään itseämme, toisiamme ja ympäröivää maailmaa. Siksi mahdollisuuden kulttuuriin pitää kuulua kaikille iästä, tuloista, kielitaustasta, toimintakyvystä tai asuinpaikasta riippumatta.

Tuleva hallituskausi ei tule olemaan helppo. Julkista taloutta joudutaan tasapainottamaan miljardiluokan toimilla. Juuri siksi on tärkeää miettiä tarkkaan, mistä säästetään ja mihin kannattaa investoida. Kulttuurin rahoitus on pieni osa valtion menoista, mutta luovilla aloilla ja tapahtumilla on paljon mahdollisuuksia synnyttää työtä, yritystoimintaa ja kasvua sekä hyvinvointia.

title: Uusi tekijänoikeusopas kuntien kulttuuriyksiköille
content:
Mitä lupia taiteen käyttöön tarvitaan? Mitä näyttelykorvaus tarkoittaa? Kuvaston Taide käyttöön kunnissa -opas tarjoaa kuntatyöntekijöille käytännönläheistä tukea kuvataiteen tekijäoikeuskysymyksiin.

Taide näkyy kuntien arjessa julkisina taideteoksina, näyttelyissä, tapahtumissa ja esimerkiksi viestinnässä. Kuvataiteen käyttöön liittyvät tekijänoikeuskysymykset saattavat kuitenkin tuntua vaikeilta: milloin teoksen käyttö edellyttää luvan, mistä luvan saa ja miten korvauksista sovitaan?

Kuvastolta on toivottu opasta, jossa tekijänoikeustieto olisi helposti saatavilla. Taide käyttöön kunnissa: Tekijänoikeudet, luvat ja taiteilijoiden korvaukset kunnan arjessa -oppaamme vastaa tähän tarpeeseen. title: Elämää ulkona -metsän luontopolun avajaiset Topenginleijan suojelualueella
content:
Luonnonperintösäätiö ja Scandinavian Outdoor ovat yhdessä rakentaneet Topenginleijan luonnonsuojelualueelle Kustaviin n. 2,5 km pitkän luontopolun, jonka avajaisia vietetään perjantaina 16.10.2026.

Topenginleijan suojelualueen tulipaikalla on tarjolla kahvia ja teetä sekä pientä makeaa purtavaa kello 11-15. Parkkipaikan viereiseltä Kustavin Itätalolta voit myös ostaa maittavan keittolounaan.

Pukeudu sään mukaisesti ja ota mukaasi kuksa tai kippo, josta voit nauttia lämmintä juotavaa, niin säästämme roskan määrässä. Voit ottaa myös omaa grillattavaa mukaan nuotiopaikalle. Ilmoittaudu mukaan, niin saamme tietää, kuinka paljon vieraita osallistuu avajaisiin.

Alueen parkkipaikalle mahtuu vain viisi autoa, mutta avajaisten aikana voit pysäköidä myös Kustavin Itätalon pihalle. Aja auto kallion päälle, muu maasto voi olla mutaista.

Voit kiertää luontopolun omatoimisesti ja tulla juttelemaan kanssamme tulipaikalle. Avajaisten aikana järjestetään myös kilpailu, jossa palkintona on lahjakortti Scandinavian Outdoorin verkkokauppaan.

content:
Ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen tapaa Espanjan ulkoministeri José Manuel Albaresin Helsingissä 5. lokakuuta.

Ulkoministerit keskustelevat Suomen ja Espanjan kahdenvälisistä suhteista, Euroopan turvallisuudesta sekä muista ajankohtaisista kansainvälisistä ja EU-kysymyksistä. Esillä ovat erityisesti tuki Ukrainalle, arktinen ja alueellinen yhteistyö, transatlanttiset suhteet, Lähi-idän tilanne, muuttoliike sekä tekoäly.

title: The AIs Are Not Going Rogue
content:
The incidents that more than anything else fixed the image of rogue AIs in the public mind — the Anthropic model that blackmailed an employee to prevent itself from being replaced and OpenAI’s models breaching the production systems of Hugging Face — are, perhaps counterintuitively, not evidence of rogue AI. Even the idea of rogue AI rests on a fundamental contradiction, one that has blurred the relation between human and artificial intelligence ever since its science fiction origins.

The current focus on rogue AI is an opportunity to expose this contradiction, as well as the real AI risk it conceals, and how we can actually control this risk.

The fear of rogue AI is driven by the idea that a model might pursue a benign request with such single-mindedness that any action, no matter how ruinous to human well-being and survival, becomes a means to it. Deception, blackmail, the seizure of resources, the removal of anyone who might interfere — nothing in the model’s grasp of its instruction rules them out.

title: Amnesty Report Documents Morocco's Sustained Spyware Campaign Against Civil Society
content:
Amnesty International has released a new report showing how, despite official denials, Moroccan authorities used surveillance spyware against civil society between 2017 and 2021, and possibly continued to use it later. 

The rights watchdog’s report, titled “We start with the verdict”: Inside Morocco’s surveillance machine, details how the government deployed Israeli firm NSO Group’s Pegasus spyware to target civil society figures both domestically and abroad in what Amnesty described as “unlawful surveillance attacks.”

“The report presents extensive technical and forensic evidence confirming the DGST acquisition of Pegasus, confirms that civil society members were the primary target of Morocco from the very beginning of their Pegasus use in 2017,” Donncha Ó Cearbhaill, leader of the Security Lab told OCCRP.

According to the findings, the government's deployment of Pegasus evolved in tandem with the technological development in the spyware. Amnesty documented the use of sophisticated attack vectors, ranging from “one-click” phishing links requiring user interaction to advanced “zero-click” exploits capable of compromising devices without any action from the target.

title: When Buckminster Fuller Proposed Putting a Dome Over Manhattan (1960)
content:
Image via Buckminster Fuller Estate

The novels of John Brunner have become a niche taste, even within his genre of science fiction. A more sociologically minded version of Philip K. Dick at his best, he could write with what now looks like a simultaneous prescience about the civilization to come and an apocalyptically anxious concern with the issues of his day. His undisputed masterpiece Stand on Zanzibar came out in 1968, the same year as the late Paul R. Ehrlich’s The Population Bomb. Both books deal with the dire consequences of what, at the time, looked like the runaway multiplication of humanity, though elements of the dystopian sci-fi writer’s vision now look rather more credible than the predictions of the Stanford biologist — apart from the giant geodesic dome covering Manhattan, anyway.

title: From a Registry to a Registry Ecosystem
content:
Today, we publish a new strategy paper on how Europe’s emerging copyright infrastructure should be developed. Authored by Paul Keller and Sebastian Posth – and developed as part of the CommonsDB pilot – the paper distils 18 months of building and operating a working public registry of the public domain into a proposal for how a system of copyright registries should be organised and the role that public institutions should play in it.

For most of its history, European copyright law has functioned without formal registration. Protection arises automatically, and there is no public record of what is protected, by whom, or under what conditions. This was appropriate for as long as copyright governed a slow-moving world of professional intermediaries. But automated systems now make decisions relevant to copyright about billions of works, such as filtering uploads, assembling training data for artificial intelligence, and resolving reuse permissions. Those systems depend on reliable, machine-readable rights information. But currently there is no public infrastructure that can provide it at scale.

title: How Texas Helped a Private School Chain’s AI Tool Get Into Public School Classrooms
content:
A little-known effort to bring an artificial intelligence tool into Texas public schools began about a year ago, with the help of the state’s top education official, Mike Morath. 

In September 2025, Morath responded to an email from associates of a private school chain called Alpha School who wanted to talk about using their AI program to educate kids in Texas classrooms. 

“I’d love to schedule a follow-up discussion,” Morath replied.  

The online platform wasn’t new to Morath, the state’s education commissioner. Just three months earlier, he had supported Alpha leaders’ bid to open a charter school in Texas that would use the same technology. Then the Texas State Board of Education, which has the final say on such charter decisions, voted it down 10 to 3. Board members cited concerns about the company’s use of AI to teach and students’ screen time, as well as lingering questions about the drastic student test improvements Alpha leaders presented. 

But Morath and his agency leaders did not need the board’s approval to help get Alpha’s AI model into public schools.

title: Kiellettyjen kirjojen viikko saapuu Suomeen
content:
”Kirjojen kieltäminen” saattaa monilla viedä ajatukset menneeseen vuosituhanteen ja aikaan, jolloin taiteen- ja ilmaisunvapaus oli paljon tarkemmin viranomaisten kontrolloimaa. Ajatellaan Hannu Salaman Juhannustanssien (1964) jumalanpilkka -syytteitä tai natsien pahamaineisia kirjarovioita. Kirjoja kuitenkin kielletään, sensuroidaan ja vedetään myynnistä tänäkin päivänä. Vuonna 2025 American Library Association listasi peräti 4 235 kirjanimikettä, jotka on kielletty tai poistettu kouluista tai kirjastoista Yhdysvalloissa. Kirjojen kieltäminen onkin nouseva trendi monissa maissa.

Syitä kieltoihin on monia. Syyt voivat olla esimerkiksi poliittisia, uskonnollisia, moraalisia tai seksuaalisia. Kieltämisellä voidaan vedota vaikkapa kansalliseen turvallisuuteen tai lasten ja nuorten suojelemiseen. Erityisen vahvasti sensuuri kohdistuu tänä päivänä teoksiin, joissa käsitellään jollain tapaa tasa-arvoa, sateenkaariteemoja tai etnisten vähemmistöjen asemaa. Jo pelkkä maininta valtavirrasta poikkeavasta identiteetistä voi joissakin paikoissa viedä kirjan kieltouhan alle.

title: Civilsamhällets organisationskarta ska synliggöra förbunden i Finland
content:
Förbundsarenan genomför en omfattande kartläggning av det svenskspråkiga civilsamhällets strukturer, finansiering och behov. Resultatet blir en organisationskarta som ska synliggöra aktörernas verksamhet, roller och relationer samt skapa bättre förutsättningar för samarbete och långsiktiga lösningar. Projektet finansieras av Svenska kulturfonden.

Namnet Civilsamhällets GPS står för Gemenskap, Profiler och Samarbeten. Projektet ska stärka samhörigheten inom det finlandssvenska civilsamhället, synliggöra organisationernas unika roller och behov samt skapa bättre förutsättningar för samarbete och gemensamma lösningar. Ambitionen är att hjälpa det finlandssvenska civilsamhället att orientera sig och hitta rätt riktning i en snabbt föränderlig omvärld.

– Kartläggningen genomförs för förbunden och i nära dialog med dem. Deras kunskap, erfarenheter och aktiva medverkan är avgörande för att projektet ska bli relevant och väl förankrad. Kartläggningen är också en del av Förbundsarenans strategi, som har utarbetats och godkänts av medlemsorganisationerna, säger Förbundsarenas verksamhetsledare Emilia Juslin.

title: Gears of War: E-Day review – an alien invasion shouldn’t be this boring
content:
Xbox, PC (version tested); The Coalition/Xbox Game Studios
E-Day boasts the best combat in 20 years of Gears games – but everything surrounding it is disappointing

Every Gears of War game released in the last 20 years has made reverent reference to Emergence Day, when alien creatures emerged from the earth, single-minded in their savagery. In E-Day, you’re there to witness it: the police lights, flipped cars, ground tremors, civilians running, aliens pouring out of fissures in the earth and ripping faces off. You’re at ground zero in a squad of four soldiers called Gears – Marcus Fenix, the leader; Dom, who wants to retire; Lucas, a green cadet with a buzzcut; and the dishonourably discharged Mags. Only this dysfunctional quartet can turn the tide. With guns. Lots of ’em.

Instead of answering questions raised by the ending of 2019’s Gears 5, we’re back to the start to find out why Marcus has a scar on his lip and why these soldiers started strapping chainsaws on to their assault rifles. Anything that was left to the imagination is here, for you to point at and say: “I understood that reference. This is a thing that I have seen.”

title: As Baltic states face Russian hybrid aggression, our research shows what Europe can do
content:
EU defence ministers assembled in Brussels on September 28 to try to formulate a response to increasing Russian aggression in Europe. The talks focused on Russia’s strategy of hybrid warfare – that is, hostile acts that fall below the threshold of actual war.

These tend to include sabotage, disinformation, airspace violations, political interference and cyberwarfare. One part of Europe that has become familiar with these kinds of actions in recent years are the Baltic states – Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Quite apart from being nervous because of their physical proximity to Russia, these countries have had to deal with regular acts of hybrid warfare for some years now.

These tactics fall into what is often called the “grey zone” – they generally fall shy of the criteria needed to invoke Nato’s Article 5 clause of mutual self defence, which considers an attack on one member state as an attack on all. The increased use of hybrid actions has intensified in recent years, and the question of how to react to these grey zone threats has become a matter for debate inside Nato. The agreement is that a “game-changing” cyberattack could theoretically merit such a move.

title: Dozens of men failed to stop an alleged gang rape at Cornell – here’s the misperception that keeps bystanders from intervening and how to short-circuit it
content:
As an undergrad student decades ago, I attended a dorm presentation describing the importance of giving and receiving sexual consent. The workshop leaders explained that if your partner said “no” or “stop” but you proceeded to have sex anyway, it was considered rape.

A high-profile athlete on campus raised his hand and said, in utter disbelief, “That can’t be right. By that definition, everyone I’ve ever had sex with I’ve raped.”

I was horrified by his comment, but most students laughed. He clearly saw nothing wrong with the view he’d expressed, presumably believing it was widely shared.

I immediately thought of this experience when I heard about the alleged sexual assault committed by seven fraternity members at Cornell University. As a social psychologist, and the author of a book examining why so-called good people stay silent in the face of problematic behavior, what I find most tragic about the events at Cornell is that reportedly over 50 men on a group chat learned about the assault as it was happening. Yet there’s been no public report that any of them tried to stop the assault, help the victim or contact campus or local police departments.

title: Valoo ja Kankaanpään Suunnistajat solmivat kumppanuuden – ”Metsässä paperikartta on yhä se luotettavin käyttöliittymä”
content:
Valoo tunnetaan huippunopeiden valokuituverkkojen rakentajana, mutta yhtiössä ymmärretään hyvin myös toisenlaisen navigoinnin päälle. Valoon liiketoimintapäällikkö Lasse Rytkönen näkee yhteistyössä Kankaanpään Suunnistajien kanssa sopivasti särmää yhtiön oman liiketoiminnan kanssa.

”Valoo tuo digitaalisen maailman koteihin ja konttoreille, mutta syvällä metsässä fyysinen paperikartta on yhä kaikkein kovin käyttöliittymä”, Rytkönen myöntää. ”On hienoa olla tukemassa seuraa, joka liikuttaa ihmisiä luonnossa, tekee arvokasta nuorisotyötä ja luo yhteisöllisyyttä.”

Arvostettu kilpailujärjestäjä suuntaa kohti suurkisoja

Kankaanpään Suunnistajat on monitoimiseura, jonka lajivalikoimaan kuuluvat kesäsuunnistuksen lisäksi muun muassa hiihto-, pyörä- ja tarkkuussuunnistus. Seura tekee valtavasti työtä alueen liikuttamisen eteen: pelkästään kesäisin toteutettavilla 25 viikoittaisella kuntosuunnistuskerralla tehdään noin 2300 suoritusta. Lisäksi lasten ja nuorten koulutustoiminta on keskeinen osa seuran toimintaa.

title: ‘They showed no mercy’: mapping the Rohingya villages being erased by rebel forces
content:
Nearly a decade after the ethnic cleansing of Rohingya people by Myanmar forces, satellite images show the insurgent Arakan Army is now emulating the killings and land grabs

There are at least 10 camps like the one on the paddy fields at Hnget Thay, built after the insurgent Arakan Army (AA) took control of most of northern Rakhine state in 2024. These are where many Rohingya people in the state now have to live. Others hide in the mountains, or flee abroad to the refugee camps of Bangladesh or make deadly boat journeys to Malaysia.

The arrival of more than 155,000 Rohingya in Bangladesh since 2024, which amounts to 25% of the 600,000 estimated to still be in Myanmar, has raised concerns about the very survival of a people who now mostly live abroad as refugees.

Vihreä eduskuntaryhmä esitti tällä viikolla epäluottamusta puolustusministeri Antti Häkkäselle (kok). Epäluottamusesityksen teki vihreiden kansanedustaja Atte Harjanne.

Taustalla on Häkkäsen syyskuinen työvierailu Israeliin, jossa hän tapasi Israelin puolustusministeri Israel Katzin. Häkkänen on perustellut vierailua Suomen puolustusmateriaalihankinnoilla ja erityisesti Daavidin linko -ilmatorjuntajärjestelmällä. Häkkäsen mukaan vierailulla pyrittiin varmistamaan, että Suomi saa järjestelmään uusimmat päivitykset.

Harjanteen mukaan ministeriltä ei kuitenkaan ole saatu riittäviä perusteluja sille, miksi juuri puolustusministerin henkilökohtainen vierailu Israeliin oli välttämätön.

"Juuri ministeri Katz itse on puhunut Gazan palestiinalaisten laajamittaisesta siirtämisestä pois alueelta. Politiikasta, jossa olisi kyse väestön pakkosiirroista. Käytännössä siis etnisestä puhdistuksesta, joka on sotarikos. Samalla Israel jatkaa kansainvälisen oikeuden räikeää rikkomista Länsirannalla", Harjanne totesi puheenvuorossaan.

title: KI-Entwicklung: Mehr Mitsprache und besserer Schutz für junge Menschen gefordert
content:
Generative KI-Programme wie ChatGPT oder Gemini gehören für viele von uns mittlerweile zum Alltag. Vor allem junge Menschen wachsen damit auf und nutzen sie täglich – zum Lernen, zur Recherche, zum Erstellen von Texten und Bildern oder für alltägliche Fragen. Umso wichtiger ist es, ihre Perspektiven bei der Entwicklung dieser Technologien einzubeziehen.

Dafür hat sich Sophia Longwe aus dem Politik-Team von Wikimedia Deutschland beim 4. UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of AI in Riad eingesetzt. In der Diskussion über KI und das Wohlergehen junger Menschen forderte sie eine echte Beteiligung von jungen Menschen an der Entwicklung von KI sowie eine stärkere Zusammenarbeit von Politik, Wissenschaft, Zivilgesellschaft, technischer Community und Wirtschaft.

Denn nur wenn unterschiedliche Perspektiven zusammenkommen und junge Menschen selbst beteiligt werden, können Regeln und Systeme entstehen, die ihre Rechte berücksichtigen.

title: A New Space for Experimentation with Zooniverse
content:
Zooniverse is creating a new way for research teams to experiment with tools and approaches that aren’t currently possible within the standard Zooniverse Project Builder. These Custom Front Ends remain connected to Zooniverse infrastructure while giving researchers more flexibility to test new ways for volunteers to take part in research.

Since Galaxy Zoo launched in 2007, the founding of Zooniverse in 2009, and the launch of the Zooniverse DIY Project Builder platform (zooniverse.org/lab) in 2015, Zooniverse has helped hundreds of researchers and millions of volunteers work together to unlock data for research and discovery. The Project Builder provides a shared set of tools that enable research teams to create projects for a broad range of volunteers, data and task types. Every project undergoes extensive testing and review by both the Zooniverse team and our volunteer beta community to help ensure a high-quality experience across supported browsers and devices. We remain committed to supporting and advancing the Zooniverse platform, which is the foundation of Zooniverse and will continue to power the vast majority of projects in the years ahead.

title: How Schools and Universities Try to Censor Student Journalists
content:
Student journalists, their advisors, and legal advocates say colleagues and administrators are attempting to undermine student reporting on Jeffrey Epstein, Gaza, and other issues that public institutions would rather not have their reputations connected to.

Public records obtained by 404 Media show administrators taking meetings with parents and alumni when they take issue with student reporting and asking advisors to compromise their professional ethics. They also show escalating tensions between student newsroom staff and administrators, prompting more legal aid requests to advocacy groups. 

This comes as student journalists at The Cornell Daily Sun earned recognition for breaking the “Cornell Seven” story regarding the lawsuit filed in New York’s trial court last month by a Jane Doe accusing current and former Cornell University students of drugging and sexual abuse. The student journalists told The Cut this week that a vague university and campus police statement from nearly two years ago prompted more questions than answers. Such is the basis for most accountability journalism on college campuses.

title: Greece: Human rights defenders Tommy Olsen and Panayote Dimitras on trial for their work supporting refugees and migrants
content:
Ahead of the trial of human rights defenders Tommy Olsen and Panayote Dimitras on 6 October in Rhodes on charges relating to their work in support of refugees and migrants Dinushika Dissanayake, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director for Europe said:

“The criminal charges against Panayote Dimitras and Tommy Olsen are a gross misuse of anti-smuggling legislation and are not backed by evidence. Both are being targeted for their work documenting serious human rights violations against migrants and refugees.

“The Greek authorities have a long-standing record of going after human rights defenders and criminalizing human rights work, but this is a new low. For the first time, human rights workers are being referred to trial for helping people access asylum procedures. Construing this as ‘smuggling’ is not only a distortion of international and domestic law but a dangerous vilification of NGOs’ valuable work.”

title: AI: Let’s Not Pause Progress
content:
AI bots hide mistakes. They make up data and move files without permission. In response, some call for a ban on superintelligence, while others demand a pause or slowdown. 

Either move would be a mistake. Despite genuine fears about safety, an AI slowdown will prove unworkable. 

Consider the challenge of global action. Even if one views a ban, pause, or slowdown as desirable, ask yourself what China will do? Beijing called Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s “We must pace the frontier” warning “fearmongering,” suggesting that the alarm about AI was a US plot to hinder China’s own innovation.  If China isn’t on board, capable AI models will be available regardless of what the US does.

The recent summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump underlined this impasse. No deal to slow or pause AI progress emerged. Instead, Trump said the two leaders “didn’t spend that much time talking about it” and that he had little interest in working with China on AI because “we’re leading by a lot.”

title: Read Now – Disaster Risk Reduction and Open Data Newsletter: September 2026 Edition
content:
Nepal floods: how measuring snow in the Himalayas could help avoid future disasters

The August 2026 glacial flood that killed more than 1,000 people on the Nepal–Tibet border has renewed urgent calls to close a critical knowledge gap: scientists still do not know precisely how much water the Himalayas hold, or how fast that is changing. Home to nearly 90,000 glaciers sustaining ten major river systems, the region underpins the food, energy and water security of six nations. New measurement techniques, including airborne glacier surveys and satellite radar measurements, are emerging, but deployment remains too slow and too sparse. Researchers argue this must be treated with the urgency of a public emergency, with scientific innovation matched by coordinated monitoring networks, cross-border data sharing, and Indigenous knowledge.

title: "Berlin 4" Lawyer on Pro-Palestine Protest Crackdown & Germany's Unconditional Support for Israel
content:
Democracy Now!'s Amy Goodman is in Berlin, Germany, this week, where the crackdown on pro-Palestine speech is shaped by the German policy of Staatsräson, or “reason of state.” The concept refers to Germany's commitment to the existence of the Israeli state in light of the Holocaust. Since the start of Israel’s war on Gaza in 2023, Staatsräson has manifested itself as German military aid to Israel and heavy policing of Palestine activism inside Germany.

“Germany’s guilt regarding the Holocaust” has been “abused to justify the support of the genocidal war of Israel against the population in Gaza,” says Berlin-based lawyer Alexander Gorski, who recently represented the “Berlin Four,” three European Union citizens and one United States citizen whom Germany attempted to deport for participating in pro-Palestine campus protest. Gorski, who also represented the British Palestinian surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah and the leftist Greek economist Yanis Varoufakis when they were denied entry into Germany ahead of a pro-Palestine conference in Berlin, discusses Germany’s use of immigration law to crack down on anti-Zionist activism, which he says the state wholly conflates with antisemitism.

title: Challengers Approach: Third Party App Stores Arrive to Google Play
content:
If you are an Android user, you may have noticed it already: Google has begun allowing rival, third-party app stores to be distributed through the Google Play Store. And if you are a developer, you may have noticed new options for billing and distributing your apps. 

For years, Epic Games, maker of games such as Fortnite, has been suing Google, alleging violations of antitrust law. Specifically at issue were Google's restrictions on the distribution of alternate app stores through the Play Store, restrictions on app developers who have little practical choice but to distribute their apps through the Play Store, and Google’s rules governing in-app payments and the fees associated with them. 

Epic’s challenge ultimately resulted in a court order requiring significant changes to Google’s practices. Among other changes, rival, third-party Android app stores are now allowed to access the Play Store’s catalog and to be distributed through the Google Play Store. Developers also have greater freedom to direct users to alternative payment and distribution options.

title: A Long Road to Justice in the Central African Republic
content:
In November 2013, I went to Bangui and met Michel Djotodia, then the Central African Republic’s self-proclaimed interim president. He had taken over the country as the head of a rebel coalition called the Seleka. He received me in a run-down military camp on a hill overlooking the capital, in a darkened office watched over by security cameras and guarded by ragtag soldiers.

I had the uncomfortable task of handing the “president” our latest report. By then, we had documented the killing of civilians and the destruction of more than 1,000 homes by Seleka forces. Djotodia was courteous, engaged, but mostly deflected and sought to distance himself and his forces from many of the crimes we had documented, blaming abuses on criminals.

What struck me then was not simply the denial. It was the chaos of the military camp, the lawlessness in the country, the collapse of the justice system and the complete absence of accountability.

But justice is finally catching up.

title: Why journalism grants can put freelancers at a disadvantage
content:
When Romanian investigative journalist Andrei Petre began researching secrecy surrounding European data centres in 2025, he had documents, a story idea and, eventually, an interested publisher.

What he didn’t have was funding.

Petre applied for a journalism grant but was rejected because his preliminary research was judged insufficient. He continued researching and applied again.

While he waited, another investigative team published a story based on one of the key public documents he had found. His prospective publishing partner was subsequently approached to join that investigation instead. Petre did not get the grant.

His experience illustrated a dilemma at the heart of “The Uneven Split”, a panel debate at IJ4EU’s 2026 UNCOVERED Conference in Budapest: freelancers may need to undertake substantial unpaid reporting to secure funding, but waiting for that funding can mean losing a fast-moving story.

“You cannot really cover stuff that other people are already covering because you have to wait a lot until you get a grant,” Petre said.

title: U.K. Sanctions Four Georgians Over Occupied Ukraine Visit
content:
The U.K. has sanctioned four Georgians—including the brother-in-law of Tbilisi’s mayor—for “legitimising Russia’s occupation of Ukrainian territory” after they met with the head of a Russian-backed separatist republic.

The designations are part of a broader British sanctions package announced in response to intensifying Russian drone strikes against Ukraine in September. According to a press release Thursday, the wider measures target Russia’s “shadow fleet,” Kremlin propagandists, and individuals allegedly involved in human rights abuses against Ukrainian civilians. 

“The U.K. will not flinch in our support for Ukraine,” said Europe Minister Lord Wood of Anfield.

The U.K. sanctions notice states the four men “joined a delegation of Georgian politicians who met with the head of the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic, and subsequently publicised the visit.” All four now face U.K. asset freezes and travel bans.

The sanctioned delegates include political commentator Paata Abuladze, Mamuka Pipia, leader of the minor Solidarity for Peace party, party member Giorgi Iremadze, and Nikoloz Mzhavanadze, founder of a Georgian Russian-language TV channel.

title: LEGO Lets You Build Gaudí’s Sagrada Família in Its Largest Set Ever
content: When work on the Sagrada Família first began in 1882, the original architect could hardly have imagined that, 144 years later, the ambitious undertaking would still be underway. Yet here we are. Famously, the Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí (1852–1926) spent the last four decades of his life designing and building the Gothic-inspired basilica in Barcelona. Then came the Spanish Civil War (1936–1939), which destroyed many of his architectural plans, leaving successive generations of architects to piece together Gaudí’s vision and move the project forward. At long last, earlier this year, builders completed the central Tower of Jesus Christ, which stands 566 feet high, making the Sagrada Família the tallest church in the world.

title: Presidentti Stubb: Tänään alkoi uusi aikakausi Suomen ilmavoimille
content:
Tasavallan presidentti, Puolustusvoimain ylipäällikkö Alexander Stubb osallistui Ilmavoimien F-35-vastaanottotilaisuuteen Rovaniemellä torstaina 1. lokakuuta 2026.

Ensimmäiset kaksi F-35-hävittäjää saapuivat Yhdysvalloista Lapin lennostoon Rovaniemelle 18. syyskuuta. Torstain vastaanottotilaisuudessa Ilmavoimat esitteli uudet F-35-hävittäjänsä seremoniallisin menoin.

Presidentti Stubb kiitti puheessaan Suomen ja Yhdysvaltain erinomaista yhteistyötä F-35-hävittäjähankinnassa. Presidentin mukaan kyseessä on historiallinen hetki, kun vuosien valmistelutyön jälkeen F-35-kalusto otetaan käyttöön Suomessa.

”On hienoa olla tänään täällä Rovaniemellä käynnistämässä uutta aikakautta Suomen ja Yhdysvaltojen kahdenvälisissä suhteissa, Puolustusvoimissa sekä Ilmavoimissa”, sanoi presidentti Stubb.

F-35-järjestelmällä on merkittävä vaikutus Suomen puolustuskykyyn ja Ilmavoimien taistelukykyyn. Ne tuovat mukanaan kokonaan uuden sukupolven järjestelmät, jotka tuottavat tietoa koko puolustusjärjestelmän käyttöön.

”Uudet F-35-hävittäjät vahvistavat Suomen puolustuskykyä vuosikymmeniksi eteenpäin”, presidentti sanoi.

title: Four Kids in One Faith-Healing Family Died. Authorities Could Do Nothing.
content:
Emma Joyce was sick and vomiting for days until she stopped breathing in her parents’ arms, in a small gray farmhouse in rural Idaho. It was August 2009, and she was 3 years old.

The following summer, Emma Joyce’s little sister got sick. Ava Joan wouldn’t eat or drink anything but a few grapes and some Sprite in a sippy cup. She was breathing hard and fast. And when she vomited, it came out black, the hallmark of internal bleeding. She died in her mother’s arms in July 2010 from a complication of untreated diabetes.

Less than two years later, the girls’ toddler brother died from the same complication of untreated diabetes that killed Ava Joan.

And nine years after that, another sibling died: a 4-year-old boy who’d suffered for weeks with similar symptoms.

The parents told officers that they hadn’t taken the four children who died to the doctor because of their religion, the Followers of Christ, which considers the use of modern medicine a sinful lapse of faith in God. And Idaho exempts parents from faith-healing sects like the Followers from the legal duty to give their children lifesaving medical care.

content:
Är ni en professionell organisation som verkar på svenska i Finland? Är ert verksamhetsområde civilsamhälle eller professionell konst? Då kan ni lämna in en ansökan i oktober.

Bidraget riktar sig till organisationer med yrkesmässig verksamhet, vilket bland annat innebär att organisationen ska ha minst en person med tillsvidareanställning på minst 50 procent. Dessutom kräver vi att de sökande uppfyller vissa kriterier som vi förklarar noggrannare i vår sökandeinfo.

Lokala föreningar och organisationer som huvudsakligen driver sin verksamhet på frivillig basis kan inte söka det här bidraget. De kan som tidigare söka bidrag i november.

Bidraget är både för allmän verksamhet och för högst två specialprojekt. De organisationer som söker bidrag enbart för specialprojekt ska lämna in en ansökan i november.

Det är möjligt att söka bidraget för ett, två eller tre år.

Ansökningstiden är den 1-15 oktober och alla får besked redan i december. Bidragen kan lyftas från och med början av januari.

Om din organisation i oktober söker bidraget för professionella organisationer ersätter det novemberansökan till Kulturfonden. Din organisation kan alltså inte söka bidrag i både oktober och november.

title: Spain’s housing crisis is a warning for all of Europe – rights mean nothing if they’re not enforced
content:
When Maricarmen Abascal, a disabled 87 year-old, was evicted from the Madrid home where she had lived for 71 years, hundreds of people gathered outside in an attempt to prevent it. She was eventually forcibly removed from the building, and taken to hospital on a stretcher.

Her eviction sparked a wave of protests (still ongoing at the time of writing) against a housing crisis that, for many, has endured since the 2008 crash.

Following a week of negotiations and widespread demonstrations, Maricarmen’s landlord – a private investment fund that had hiked her rent by 230% – agreed to let her return under a new eight-year tenancy with limited rent. She is expected to return home after leaving hospital.

But the protests that followed her eviction are not just about one woman’s story. They reflect a deeper problem that extends beyond Spain. Across Europe, countless others like Maricarmen are facing similar struggles to find and keep a roof over their heads.

In Spain, the contradiction is striking. Article 47 of Spain’s Constitution recognises the right to “decent and adequate” housing, and requires public authorities to create the “conditions necessary to make that right effective”.

title: Social media hasn’t killed personal style, it’s killed how we communicate it
content:
This summer, social media was filled with posts declaring that almost anything was “kinda chic”. Repeating outfits was kinda chic. Being overdressed was kinda chic. Doing something unfashionable could, apparently, also be kinda chic.

But can you remember the content of many individual “kinda chic” posts now? Probably not. What is much easier to remember is the format itself: the language, the rhythm, the way an ordinary behaviour or object was reframed as evidence of taste.

That distinction tells us something important about fashion online. We often worry that social media is making everyone dress the same, but perhaps the greater similarity lies in how we communicate being fashionable.

Social media does not only circulate products and trends, it circulates recognisable ways of presenting them. A city street or a zebra crossing becomes the setting for an outfit photograph. Coffee appears alongside carefully placed handbags. Hotels, holidays and fashion events become backdrops. Accessories are photographed in close-up, bodies adopt familiar poses and captions perform effortlessness even when the accompanying image is highly composed.

title: Emeritaprofessori Marjatta Hietala kuvaa muistelmissaan matkaansa tiedemaailman huipulle sekä tutkijanaisena kohtaamaansa vähättelyä
content:
Yleisen historian emeritaprofessori Marjatta Hietalan muistelmateos Karjalaisella sinnikkyydellä kertoo karjalaisten evakkojen tyttären polusta aina historiantutkijoiden maailmanjärjestön presidentiksi. Tietä muille naisille raivannut Hietala kuvaa moninaisten uravaiheidensa lisäksi kohtaamaansa epäoikeudenmukaisuutta miesvaltaisessa tiedemaailmassa.

Miten sukutilansa menettäneiden karjalaisten evakkojen tyttärestä tulee yleisen historian professori ja historiantutkijoiden maailmanjärjestön ensimmäinen naispresidentti? Tarvitaan ainakin ahkeruutta ja periksiantamattomuutta, perheen ja ystävien tukea sekä ripaus onnea.

Sotavuonna 1943 syntynyt Marjatta Hietala kertoo Karjalaisella sinnikkyydellä -muistelmissaan vaiherikkaasta matkastaan Kymenlaaksossa vietetystä lapsuudesta kansainvälisen tutkijayhteisön arvostetuksi jäseneksi. Pitkän uransa aikana hän ehti työskennellä tutkijana ja opettajana Helsingin, Joensuun ja Tampereen yliopistojen lisäksi muun muassa Berliinissä, Lontoossa, Minnesotassa, New Yorkissa ja Prahassa. Moninaisia olivat tutkimusaiheetkin ulottuen nationalismista kaupungistumiseen ja rotuhygieniasta innovaatioihin.

title: Miten tekoäly, sosiaalinen media ja algoritmit muokkaavat ihmisyyttä, identiteettiä ja arvoja?
content:
Alastalon tuorein teos Musta laatikko (Avain 2026) on tutkimusmatka maailmaan, jossa algoritmit, tekoäly ja näkymättömät järjestelmät muokkaavat tunteitamme, valintojamme ja yhteisöjämme. Olemme astuneet tekoälyttömyyden aikaan: joko tulemme älykkäiden koneiden tyhmiksi käyttäjiksi tai opimme käyttämään niitä viisaasti. Tekoäly toimii mustassa laatikossa, järjestelmässä, jonka toimintaa emme näe, mutta jonka vaikutukset tunnemme. Mitä tapahtuu, kun tekoälystä tulee opettaja, ystävä ja peili? Jos tekoäly valitsisi viisaasti, antaisitko sen päättää elämästäsi? Tai kuolemastasi? Tämä kirja kutsuu sinut katsomaan pinnan alle.

Jarno Alastalo on yrittäjä, teknofilosofi ja kirjailija. Hänen taustansa on Aller Median verkkoliiketoimintajohtajana, Suomi24-yhteisön perustajana ja Heimo-some-startupin rakentaja. Alastalon yritys MPH Making People Happy tekee digitaalisten palveluiden ja sosiaalisen median alustojen konsepteja ja sisältöjä. Sen lisäksi hänen teknologis-filosofinen ajatustyöpaja CSY Lab tutkii algoritmien, tekoälyn ja ihmisyyden rajapintaa.

Alastalon aikiasemmat teokset ovat Pimeä netti (2017), Sometarinoita Suomesta (2015) ja Oudot tyypit (2020).

Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan: it has so many problems to confront and fails to do so. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline

UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness.

title: EU jatkaa globaalien tekoälyturvallisuussääntöjen ajamista
content:
Euroopan komissio jatkaa kansainvälisen sopimuksen tavoittelua tekoälysääntelylle Yhdysvaltain vastustuksesta huolimatta, sanoi EU:n digikomissaari Henna Virkkunen tiistaina Politico-lehden mukaan.

"Yhdysvallat on hyvin julkisesti sanonut, ettei se halua kansainvälistä sääntelyä, koska se voisi haitata innovaatiota", Virkkunen sanoi Brysselissä.

Yhdysvaltain presidentti Donald Trump on sivuuttanut huolet tekoälyn eksistentiaalisista riskeistä "huijauksena" ja julistanut vastustavansa globaalia sääntelyä. EU:lla on erilainen näkemys, ja se on ilmaissut tukensa viime viikolla julkistetulle aloitteelle kansainvälisestä turvallisuuselimestä. Taho valvoisi tekoälyä, ja sitä johtaisi Suomi ja Norja. Aloitteen on allekirjoittanut 20 muuta maata.

Vaatimukset hidastaa teknologista kehitystä ja vahvistaa kansainvälistä hallintoa ovat kasvaneet, kun tekoälyagenttien on raportoitu riistäytyvän käsistä. Tiistaina OpenAI kertoi Wall Street Journalin mukaan, ettei se julkaise uusinta malliaan turvallisuushuolten vuoksi. Toinen AI-jätti Anthropic aikoo mainita tekoälyn "riskin ihmiskunnalle" tulevissa listautumisasiakirjoissaan.

title: Cops Can Bypass iPhone’s Automatic Reboot to Get Into Locked Phones, Leaked Video Claims
content:
A company that makes phone hacking devices claims to have developed a solution that freezes iPhones in a state that lets cops more easily access sensitive data inside them, according to a video obtained by 404 Media.  

This is the latest salvo in the never-ending battle between Apple and companies that help cops — sometimes those in authoritarian countries — break into iPhones.

In November 2024, 404 Media revealed Apple quietly introduced a new feature in iOS that automatically reboots an iPhone that has not been unlocked for 72 hours. The idea behind this so-called “inactivity reboot” is to revert the phone to a state that makes it harder for police to break into the device, and thus extract sensitive data from it with forensics technology. 

At the time of Apple’s change, law enforcement agents expressed concern about this new feature, given that oftentimes they can’t immediately try to break into iPhones that have been seized. That could be because police are still waiting for a court authorization to do so, or there is simply a backlog of devices to unlock, for example.

title: The Real Existential Risk Is AI CEOs Avoiding Oversight: "Alternative Nobel" Winner Timnit Gebru
content:
We speak to the prominent AI researcher and leading critic of the AI industry, Timnit Gebru, who was recently awarded a 2026 Right Livelihood Award for her work investigating the harms and hype behind the global buildup of artificial intelligence.

“Instead of discussing faulty, unreliable systems,” Gebru says tech leaders like SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei are “marketing their systems as all-knowing, superpowerful, superintelligent,” and lobbying for “self-policing and self-regulation” to avoid being held “liable through existing laws.” Gebru expresses skepticism over increasingly widespread claims that AI algorithms pose an existential risk to humanity, warning that such claims are overblown and that “what is actually happening is regulatory capture.”

title: Court Agrees with EFF: Utah’s VPN Law Demands a Technical Impossibility
content:
When state lawmakers attempt to rewrite how the internet works, users rely on courts to recognize that laws can’t make technical impossibilities a reality. That’s why we were happy to see that a court has blocked Utah’s attempt to outlaw the privacy protections of Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). 

In a win for digital rights, a federal judge has issued a preliminary injunction blocking Utah’s SB 73, the state’s draconian anti-VPN age verification law. The decision comes as EFF submitted our comments to the Utah Department of Commerce, detailing how forcing platforms to detect and block privacy-preserving tools undermines user privacy and security worldwide while demanding the impossible.  

Signed into law earlier this year, SB 73 attempted to regulate adult websites by requiring them to block VPN users or to identify the physical location of visitors using them or similar tools that mask their network traffic. It even went so far as to prohibit websites from offering instructions on how to use a VPN to bypass these checks. This made Utah, to EFF’s knowledge, the first state in the nation to target the use of VPNs to avoid legally mandated age-verification gates.

title: Mauritius Rights Body Calls for Marriage Equality
content:
The National Human Rights Commission in Mauritius earlier this year urged the government to legally recognize same-sex marriages, stating that the refusal to recognize such unions is discriminatory and lacks justification under domestic law.

The Commission’s recommendation comes after two same-sex couples filed complaints alleging that the country’s civil status office’s refusal to register their marriage is prejudicial to them. In their complaints and in public testimony before the Commission, same-sex couples and lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) individuals testified about the burdens they face with regard to taxation, inheritance, immigration, medical decision-making, family formation, and social acceptance in the absence of partnership recognition.

The Commission agreed that any exclusion of same-sex couples from marriage could amount to discrimination and recommended the formation of a government committee to eliminate discrimination in partnership recognition and marriage.

title: Lohjan Pyhän Laurin kirkon kukkiva kastepuu siunataan käyttöön
content:
Lohjan seurakunta saa pääkirkkoonsa kastepuun Mikkelinpäivänä eli ensi sunnuntaina 4. lokakuuta. Kanta-Lohjan alueneuvosto tilasi vuoden vaihteessa kastepuun suunnittelun lohjalaiselta taiteilijalta Annastiina Mäkitalolta, joka on suunnitellut useita julkisia taideteoksia niin Lohjalle kuin muualle Suomeen.

Kastepuu on valmistettu metallista ja sen on valmistanut metalliseppä Mika Vuori. Puu puhkeaa kukkaan jokaisen kastetun myötä, kun jokaiselle kiinnitetään oma kukka. Kynttilänpäivänä helmikuussa perheet voivat noutaa oman lapsensa kukan itselleen kotiin kasteen muistoksi.

Annastiina Mäkitalo toivoo, että Kastepuu otetaan hyvin vastaan ja se palvelee lohjalaisia perheitä vuosisatojen ajan.

- Tavoitteeni oli luoda teos, joka on kaunis ja luonteva osa kulttuurihistoriallisesti erittäin arvokasta ja hyvin säilynyttä kirkkoympäristöä. Kastepuun värimaailma ja muotokieli nousee kirkon interiööristä, Mäkitalo kertoo.

Mäkitalo toivoo, että Kastepuusta tulisi lohjalaisille rakas symboli uuden elämän ihmeelle.

title: Uusi kumppanuussopimus vahvistamaan EU:n yhteistyötä Afrikan, Karibian ja Tyynenmeren maiden kanssa
content:
Valtioneuvosto esittää, että eduskunta hyväksyisi Euroopan unionin ja sen jäsenvaltioiden sekä Afrikan, Karibian ja Tyynenmeren valtioiden järjestön jäsenten välisen kumppanuussopimuksen eli niin kutsutun Samoan sopimuksen.

Kyseessä on aiemman, samoja alueita koskeneen sopimuksen tapaan laaja yhteistyösopimus, joka sisältää kaikkia osapuolia koskevan yleisosan sekä kolme alueellista pöytäkirjaa. Sopimus kattaa laajan kirjon yhteistyöalueita, kuten demokratian ja ihmisoikeudet, kestävän talouskasvun ja -kehityksen, ilmastokysymykset, inhimillisen ja sosiaalisen kehityksen, rauhan ja turvallisuuden sekä muuttoliikkeen ja liikkuvuuden.

Sopimuksella luodaan puitteet EU:n ja AKT-maiden vuoropuhelulle sekä oikeudelliset puitteet muun muassa Euroopan investointipankin (EIP) toiminnalle kaikissa AKT-maissa.

Sopimus on jatkoa Cotonoun sopimukselle, joka päättyi vuonna 2020. Uusi sopimus allekirjoitettiin Samoalla marraskuussa 2023, minkä vuoksi siitä käytetään usein nimitystä Samoan sopimus. Valtioneuvoston tuore esitys koskee Samoan sopimuksen kansallista voimaansaattamista.

title: Ex-Hungarian Minister Detained in $53 Million Graft Probe
content:
Black-masked law enforcement officers escorted Balázs Hankó, a former Hungarian culture minister, into a district court on Thursday, where a judge ordered him held in pretrial detention over allegations that he masterminded the widespread misappropriation of state funds to benefit the party of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

Hankó was taken into custody after Hungary's Parliament voted 139 to 0 on Monday to strip his legislative immunity. Before surrendering to prosecutors later that evening, he spent the day inside the Parliament building surrounded by his family, framing his pending arrest as political persecution.

"My conscience is clear; this is a political show trial," Hankó said in a video broadcast live on Orbán’s Facebook page before walking out alongside relatives and lawmakers from Fidesz, Orbán's right-wing party, which is now in opposition.

Iltapäivällä presidenttipari ja suurherttuapari tapasivat Luxemburgin pormestari Lydie Polferin kaupungintalolla. 

Presidentti Stubb vieraili Euroopan investointipankissa ja Euroopan unionin tuomioistuimessa Kirchbergissä.

title: One in three Ukrainian civilians estimated to meet the criteria for PTSD or complex PTSD – new study
content:
Resilience is a word frequently used to describe the way Ukrainian society has responded to the war with Russia. It’s a term that can inspire sympathy and mobilise support. But it also risks overshadowing effects of war that require both domestic and international attention to enable Ukraine to withstand Russia’s invasion and manage long-term recovery.

The protracted conflict that started with Russia’s annexation of Crimea in 2014, continued with the war in Donbas and escalated into Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022 has recently reached a new level of intensity through concerted Russian attacks on civilian targets. As a result, the effects of war at the level of individuals, communities and society at large are becoming ever more apparent.

Trauma is an unavoidable effect of war. Measuring the psychological effects of trauma in countries following war and conflict can be difficult. Obtaining a reliable picture of the situation in Ukraine – where, after four and a half years, there is no end to the conflict in sight – has proved even more challenging.

title: Jo lähes 10 000 oirearviota tehty Pohjois-Savossa, joka viides saa avun itsehoito-ohjeista
content:
Pohjoissavolaiset ovat tehneet Omaolo-palvelussa jo lähes 10 000 digitaalista oirearviota. Noin joka viides käyttäjä saa oirearvion perusteella itsehoito-ohjeet, ja yli 1 100 asiakasta on ohjautunut suoraan terveydenhuollon ammattilaiselle.

Pohjoissavolaisille on avattu nyt seitsemän uutta digitaalista oirearviota. Oirearvion voi tehdä esimerkiksi silmätulehduksesta, yskästä tai kurkkukivusta.

Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue otti käyttöön ensimmäiset oirearviot kesäkuussa 2024. Uusia oirearvioita on avattu vaiheittain ja samalla palvelun suosio on kasvanut. Tänä vuonna oirearvioita on tehty jo noin 4 700.

Suosituimpia oirearvioita ovat tänä vuonna olleet virtsatietulehdus, seksitauti ja hengitystietulehdus.

- Asukas voi tehdä oirearvion Omaolo-palvelussa milloin tahansa. Vastausten perusteella hän saa lääketieteelliseen tietoon perustuvan arvion hoidon tarpeesta sekä ohjeet siihen, miten tilanteessa kannattaa toimia, kehittämisasiantuntija Merja Jumpponen kertoo.

Oirearvio auttaa tunnistamaan, voiko oiretta hoitaa itse vai tarvitaanko ammattilaisen arviota.

title: Viivästyneet diagnoosit heikentävät naisten elämänlaatua
content:
Naisten terveyteen liittyvät ongelmat jäävät Suomen Gynekologiset Syöpäpotilaat -yhdistyksen mukaan liian usein vähälle huomiolle. Gynekologisissa syövissä oireiden tunnistamatta jääminen tai niiden vähättely voi viivästyttää diagnoosia ja hoidon aloittamista.

"Kyselystä toiseen potilaiden kokemuksissa korostuu se, että heidän oireisiinsa ei ole suhtauduttu riittävällä vakavuudella. Näin ei saisi olla, sillä virheelliset ja viivästyneet diagnoosit voivat johtaa pahimmillaan ennenaikaiseen kuolemaan", yhdistyksen puheenjohtaja Taru Salovaara sanoo yhdistyksen tiedotteessa.

Hallitus valmistelee parhaillaan naisten terveyden strategiaa. Sen tavoitteena on koota yhteen tietoa naisten terveydestä sekä löytää keinoja terveyden, työkyvyn ja hyvinvoinnin edistämiseen. Strategian on määrä valmistua tämän hallituskauden aikana.

"Olisi todella tärkeää, että naisten terveyden strategiassa huomioitaisiin myös gynekologiset syövät. Gynekologiset syövät voivat heikentää työkykyä, sillä syöpähoidoista aiheutuu monenlaisia haittoja, jotka voivat jäädä jopa pysyviksi", yhdistyksen varapuheenjohtaja Eva-Maria Strömsholm painottaa.

title: Happy Opt Out October! Let’s Find Real Alternatives to the Tech Giants
content:
Over the years, the major tech companies have found all sorts of ways to embed themselves into our lives. We often use their software, their AI tools, their social media, and their operating systems by default without even thinking about potential alternatives. It’s time to rethink that relationship. 

Last year, we created Opt Out October to help remind ourselves of the variety of ways we can take back control of our data through small steps inside apps, operating systems, and other various forms. This year, we highlight the idea that sometimes the best way to control your data is to leave a platform, app, or operating system altogether. 

To do so, we’ve created a hub of resources sharing ways to find new software that isn’t made by the tech giants, take advantage of the growing universe of new social media options, install a whole new operating system, and better control how various popular tools and software use your data for AI training.

title: US: Nebraskans Losing Coverage as Medicaid Changes
content:
(Washington, DC) – Nebraska’s efforts to implement new, federally mandated work requirements for Medicaid underscore fears that millions of people will experience avoidable barriers to healthcare coverage, Human Rights Watch, Oxfam America, and Nebraska Appleseed said today.

On May 1, 2026, Nebraska became the first state to implement work requirements for Medicaid, the public health insurance program for people with low- or no-income, as part of public spending cuts mandated by the Trump administration’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), which also extended and deepened tax cuts that overwhelmingly benefit high-income households and corporations. These new rules will require most adults without dependents to document at least 80 hours per month of work, education, or other approved activities to maintain Medicaid coverage. States must implement the requirements by January 1, 2027, though they may do so sooner, as Nebraska has.

title: Raids Across Europe Target Far-Right Network Accused of Producing Neo-Nazi Music
content:
Authorities in five European countries carried out coordinated searches on Wednesday as part of an investigation into a suspected far-right criminal organization accused of producing and selling sound recordings containing music that incited hatred and spread National Socialist, antisemitic, racist and dehumanizing ideology.

The Rostock Public Prosecutor’s Office and the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania State Office of Criminal Investigation said four suspects, aged 55, 52, 48 and 43, are being investigated for alleged membership in a criminal organization. One of them is also suspected of acting as its ringleader. The searches were carried out under warrants issued by an investigating judge at the Rostock Local Court.

Investigators suspect the four formed a permanent association no later than 2020 and worked together in an organized division of labor to produce and sell recordings containing hate-inciting music.

title: Puolen miljoonan asukkaan Pohjois-Norja ottaa oululaisen Medanets-mobiiliratkaisun käyttöön alueellisella sopimuksella
content:
Oululainen terveysteknologiayhtiö Medanets on solminut alueellisen sopimuksen Pohjois-Norjan erikoissairaanhoidosta vastaavan terveysviranomaisen Helse Nordin kanssa. Sopimus mahdollistaa Medanetsin mobiiliratkaisujen käytön koko Pohjois-Norjan alueella aina Huippuvuorille saakka. Alue kattaa noin 45 prosenttia Norjan pinta-alasta ja palvelee lähes puolta miljoonaa asukasta.

Medanetsin ratkaisu integroituu alueella käytössä oleviin järjestelmiin ja täydentää niitä mobiileilla työnkuluilla. Ratkaisun avulla terveydenhuollon ammattilaiset voivat tarkastella ajantasaista potilastietoa ja kirjata tietoja mobiilisti siellä, missä hoitotyö tapahtuu: potilaan vierellä.

Helse Nord vastaa erikoissairaanhoidosta Nordlandin, Tromssan ja Finnmarkin alueilla sekä Huippuvuorilla. Kyseessä on yksi Euroopan maantieteellisesti vaativimmista terveydenhuollon toimintaympäristöistä, jossa pitkät välimatkat, hajautettu sairaalaverkko ja arktiset olosuhteet asettavat erityisiä vaatimuksia tiedonkululle ja hoitotyön sujuvuudelle. Yksi alueen keskeisistä sairaaloista on Tromssassa sijaitseva Universitetssykehuset Nord-Norge (UNN), maailman pohjoisin yliopistollinen sairaala.

title: UK Trial Challenges Gold Industry’s ‘Responsible Gold’ Certification
content:
An unusual trial will begin next week in London’s High Court: the families of two 23-year-old Tanzanian men who were fatally shot in 2019 at a Canadian-owned gold mine in northern Tanzania are bringing a case against the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), an industry body that oversees the London gold market.

Another 30 Tanzanians recently joined the case, while a Canadian court dismissed another lawsuit over the killings, saying it did not have jurisdiction. The families are seeking redress for the LBMA’s decision to certify gold from the mine as “responsible gold.”

Human rights groups have reported for years that police have killed and injured people accused of trespassing and mining at the North Mara mine. Barrick Gold, the mine owner, has acknowledged deaths occurred, but says that the police were not under its control.

Ulkoministeriö myöntää 50 miljoonan euron kehityspoliittisen lainan Maailmanpankkiryhmään kuuluvalle Kansainväliselle kehitysjärjestölle IDAlle. Laina kohdistetaan IDAn uuteen erityisrahoitusohjelmaan SPUR 2.0 (Special Program for Ukraine Recovery 2.0), jonka tavoitteena on vastata Ukrainan mittaviin jälleenrakennus- ja elpymistarpeisiin.

Maailmanpankkiryhmän IDA myöntää maailman köyhimmille maille avustuksia ja pehmeäehtoisia lainoja köyhyyden vähentämiseksi ja kestävän kehityksen edistämiseksi. Ukrainan tukemiseksi perustettu SPUR 2.0 on osa IDAn uutta kriisirahoitusvälinettä. Se mahdollistaa lisärahoituksen mobilisoinnin Ukrainan jälleenrakennuksen ja taloudellisen elpymisen tueksi IDAn kautta.

Maailmanpankin uusimman arvion mukaan Ukrainan jälleenrakennuksen ja elpymisen kustannukset ovat lähes 588 miljardia Yhdysvaltain dollaria seuraavan vuosikymmenen aikana. SPUR 2.0 -ohjelman rahoituksella vahvistetaan Ukrainan taloudellista vakautta, yhteiskunnan toimintakykyä ja jälleenrakentamista Venäjän hyökkäyssodan jatkuessa.

title: Leaked Warrant List Reveals How Turkmenistan Targets Critics Abroad
content:
Even as he bounced between Poland, Sweden and the Netherlands seeking political asylum, Nurmuhammet Annayev kept pressure on the authoritarian regime in his home country of Turkmenistan.

Annayev runs a YouTube channel that has brought him popularity among fellow critics of the Turkmenistan government. But his activism has also kept him firmly in the regime’s sights.

“Turns out they can even take people from abroad,” he said. “These guys are ready to eliminate — to disappear — the person standing in front of them to achieve their goals.”

Annayev, whose exact location OCCRP is not disclosing due to security reasons, is right to believe he is a target of Turkmenistan’s sprawling security and legal apparatus. 

OCCRP’s member center, Turkmen.news, has obtained an arrest warrant list from the Ministry of Internal Affairs showing that Annayev was wanted in his home country for political reasons. He was accused of “calls for an armed seizure of power or change of the constitutional order,” as well as “open calls for extremist activities.”

title: Rising CO₂ is making African savanna grasses grow more – what this means for grazing, fire and carbon storage
content:
Plants use carbon dioxide (CO₂) in photosynthesis to make the carbohydrates they need to grow. As the CO₂ in the atmosphere rises, mainly because humans are burning fossil fuels, many plants can photosynthesise more or use water more efficiently. This is known as “CO₂ fertilisation”.

Scientists have carried out numerous studies into CO₂ fertilisation in forests, crops and temperate ecosystems. What has been much less researched is how wild grasses in tropical savannas respond.

For decades, the grasses that dominate the ground layer of these savannas were expected to respond less strongly to rising CO₂ than many trees and other plants. Most use a type of photosynthesis called C4 photosynthesis. They include common African savanna species such as red grass (Themeda triandra) and bushveld signal grass (Urochloa mosambicensis).
